questions.question: Dr. Nadia examines a radiograph of a benign tumor. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'What is the typical radiographic appearance of a benign tumor?'
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Benign tumors generally have well-defined borders with corticalization.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will evaluate the borders of the lesion.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a radiograph of a tooth with a periapical lesion. Dr. Nadia asks him to differentiate between a granuloma and a cyst. What is the key criterion?
options: The size of the lesion (> 1.5 cm for a cyst)
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'A cyst is generally larger than a granuloma (> 1.5-2 cm).' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will measure the lesion.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph of a tooth with external resorption. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'How does external resorption appear?'
options: An irregular radiolucent area on the external root contour
A symmetrical radiolucent area centered on the canal
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'External resorption manifests as an irregular loss of substance on the external contour.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will monitor the evolution.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub performed a CBCT for implant placement. Dr. Nadia asks him to evaluate the bone height. What parameter is measured on the CBCT?
options: The available bone height from the crest to the sinus or nerve
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'CBCT allows precise measurement of available bone height.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will always perform a pre-implant CBCT.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph of a mandibular cystic lesion. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'What is the most frequent odontogenic cyst?'
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'The radicular cyst is the most frequent of the odontogenic cysts.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will look for apical lesions.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a radiograph of a patient with a malignant tumor. Dr. Nadia asks him to identify the radiographic signs. What is the key sign?
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Malignant tumors present irregular borders and bone destruction.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will refer the patient quickly.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph of an osteosarcoma. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'What is the typical radiographic appearance?'
options: A mixed radiopaque and radiolucent lesion with spicules
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Osteosarcoma presents spicules (sunburst appearance) and a mixed lesion.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will look for these signs.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a radiograph of a patient with an ossifying fibroma. Dr. Nadia asks him: 'What is the radiographic appearance of an ossifying fibroma?'
options: A radiolucent lesion with internal radiopaque areas
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Ossifying fibroma presents radiolucent areas with radiopaque islands.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will monitor the evolution.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph of a tooth with a deep cavity. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'How does a deep cavity appear on a radiograph?'
options: A radiolucent area that penetrates into the dentin
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'A cavity appears as a radiolucent (light) area that progresses into the dentin.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will evaluate the depth.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a radiograph of a patient with osteitis. Dr. Nadia asks him: 'How does alveolar osteitis appear?'
options: A diffuse radiolucent area around the alveolus
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Alveolar osteitis manifests as diffuse radiolucency around the alveolus.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will prescribe treatment.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph of a tooth with an amalgam. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'Why does amalgam appear radiopaque?'
options: Because of its high density (heavy metals)
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Amalgam contains heavy metals that absorb X-rays, appearing radiopaque (white).' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will identify restorations.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a radiograph of a patient with osteomyelitis. Dr. Nadia asks him: 'How does osteomyelitis appear on a radiograph?'
options: A radiolucent area with a sequestrum (bone separation)
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Osteomyelitis presents radiolucency with a central radiopaque sequestrum.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will prescribe urgent treatment.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph of a tooth with pulpal calcification. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'How does pulpal calcification appear?'
options: Punctate radiopaque areas in the pulp chamber
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Pulpal calcifications are radiopaque (white) areas in the canal.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will identify the calcification.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a radiograph of a patient with hypercementosis. Dr. Nadia asks him: 'How does hypercementosis appear?'
options: A radiopaque thickening of the root cementum
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Hypercementosis manifests as a radiopaque thickening of the cementum.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will monitor the evolution.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph of a tooth with ankylosis. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'What is the radiographic sign of ankylosis?'
options: Disappearance of the periodontal ligament in one area
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Ankylosis is characterized by the disappearance of the periodontal ligament.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will evaluate the ligament.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a radiograph of a patient with a dentigerous cyst. Dr. Nadia asks him: 'How does a dentigerous cyst appear?'
options: A radiolucent area around the crown of an impacted tooth
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'The dentigerous cyst appears as a radiolucency around the crown of an impacted tooth.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will monitor the evolution.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph of a tooth with an enamel lesion. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'How does enamel caries appear on a radiograph?'
options: A radiolucent area limited to the enamel
A radiolucent area that penetrates into the dentin
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Enamel caries is a radiolucent area limited to the enamel.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will monitor progression.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a radiograph of a patient with fibrosis. Dr. Nadia asks him: 'How does fibrosis appear on a radiograph?'
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Fibrosis presents radiolucency with trabeculations.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will monitor the evolution.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph of a tooth with an impacted tooth. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'What is the most frequent location of impacted canines?'
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Maxillary canines are the second most frequently impacted teeth.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will always check the canines.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a radiograph of a patient with an odontogenic tumor. Dr. Nadia asks him: 'What is the most frequent benign odontogenic tumor?'
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Odontoma is the most frequent benign odontogenic tumor.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will monitor the evolution.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph of a tooth with an apical fracture. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'How does an apical fracture appear?'
options: A thin radiolucent line at the apex level
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'An apical fracture appears as a thin radiolucent line at the apex level.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will look for this line.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a radiograph of a patient with osteodystrophy. Dr. Nadia asks him: 'How does osteodystrophy appear?'
options: A radiolucent area with bone anomalies
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Osteodystrophy manifests with bone anomalies.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will monitor the evolution.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph of a tooth with dental ankylosis. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'What is the radiographic sign of ankylosis?'
options: Disappearance of the periodontal ligament in one area
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Ankylosis is characterized by the disappearance of the periodontal ligament.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will evaluate the ligament.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a radiograph of a patient with hyperdontia. Dr. Nadia asks him: 'How does hyperdontia appear?'
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Hyperdontia manifests as a supernumerary tooth.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will identify the additional tooth.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub, after having managed complex radiology cases with Dr. Nadia, receives her congratulations. What is the next step for Dr. Ayoub?
options: Become an expert in clinical radiology and 3D imaging
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Mastery of complex cases is a valuable skill. Becoming an expert is the next step.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will train in 3D imaging.'
